Issue #7: Undefined variable in library file
Location: Line 33 in lib/usermanagement_utils.robot
Current Code:
```
Sleep  ${SETTING_WAIT_TIMEOUT}
```

Issue: Variable ${SETTING_WAIT_TIMEOUT} is not defined in this library file. It relies on the caller's context, which may cause failures if called from suites that don't define this variable.
Fix: Either define the variable in this library or import it from a common variables file:
```

*** Variables ***
${SETTING_WAIT_TIMEOUT}  30s
```
Why: Libraries should be self-contained and not depend on caller's variable scope for reliability.

Issue #4: Inconsistent Teardown Between Test Cases
Location: Lines 283-295 in redfish/managers/test_bmc_protocol_settings.robot
Current Code:

```
# Line 286 - Disable test HAS teardown
[Teardown]  Set User Account State  admin_user  ${True}

# Line 295 - Enable test has NO teardown
Enable Admin User Verify User Is Allowed To Do SSH On SOL Port
    [Documentation]  Enable admin user and verify user is allowed to login via SSH on SOL port.
    [Tags]  Enable_Admin_User_Verify_User_Is_Allowed_To_Do_SSH_On_SOL_Port
    Verify User Enable Disable And SSH Login  admin_user  Administrator  ${HOST_SOL_PORT}  ${True}
```

Issue: Only the "Disable" test has teardown. If "Enable" test fails midway, user could be left disabled, affecting subsequent tests.

Fix: Add consistent teardown to both tests:
```

Enable Admin User Verify User Is Allowed To Do SSH On SOL Port
    [Documentation]  Enable admin user and verify user is allowed to login via SSH on SOL port.
    [Tags]  Enable_Admin_User_Verify_User_Is_Allowed_To_Do_SSH_On_SOL_Port
    [Teardown]  Set User Account State  admin_user  ${True}
    
    Verify User Enable Disable And SSH Login  admin_user  Administrator  ${HOST_SOL_PORT}  ${True}
```

Why: Ensures consistent cleanup and prevents test pollution.
By Default user should be enabled, so am not adding teardown in Enable TC.
Acknowledged

Issue #2: Multiple Redfish Logins Without Session Management
```
# Line 382 in test_bmc_protocol_settings.robot
Run Keywords  Redfish.Login  AND  Enable SSH Protocol  ${True}
```

Fix Required:

```
# Option 1: Check if already logged in
${logged_in}=  Run Keyword And Return Status  Redfish.Get  /redfish/v1/SessionService/Sessions
IF  not ${logged_in}
    Redfish.Login
END
Enable SSH Protocol  ${True}

# Option 2: Remove redundant login (Suite Setup already logs in)
Enable SSH Protocol  ${True}
```

Why: Suite Setup already calls Redfish.Login at line 303. Logging in again without logout creates multiple sessions, potentially exhausting BMC session limits (typically 4-16 concurrent sessions). This could cause test failures or affect other tests.

ssue #6: No Verification of SSH Connection Failure Reason
Location: Lines 423-431 in redfish/managers/test_bmc_protocol_settings.robot
Current Code:
```
${login_status}=  Run Keyword And Return Status
...  Open Connection And Log In  host=${OPENBMC_HOST}  port=${port}
...  username=${username}  password=${OPENBMC_PASSWORD}
```

Issue: SSH connection could fail for many reasons (network down, SSH service stopped, wrong port, timeout), not just user disabled. Test would pass/fail for wrong reasons.
Fix: Add pre-checks and better error handling:
```

# Verify SSH service is running on the port first with a known-good user
${ssh_service_up}=  Run Keyword And Return Status
...  Open Connection And Log In  host=${OPENBMC_HOST}  port=${port}
...  username=${OPENBMC_USERNAME}  password=${OPENBMC_PASSWORD}  timeout=5s
Run Keyword If  ${ssh_service_up}  Close All Connections
Should Be True  ${ssh_service_up}  msg=SSH service on port ${port} is not accessible

# Now test target user authentication
${login_status}=  Run Keyword And Return Status
...  Open Connection And Log In  host=${OPENBMC_HOST}  port=${port}
...  username=${username}  password=${OPENBMC_PASSWORD}  timeout=10s
```

Why: Distinguishes between SSH service issues and user authentication issues by first verifying service is up with a known-good account.
